title: Build first-party website conversion capture and attribution
story: JVT has a working public site, automated outbound pipeline, and a canonical commercial opportunity ledger, but the public site currently converts only through a mailto link and does not provide first-party attribution. Build the smallest safe first-party workflow-intake path that lets a prospect describe a workflow problem without uploading sensitive files. Persist a durable internal submission event, attribute the source and service interest, expose conversion counts in the control panel, and hand qualified submissions into the existing inbox/opportunity/commercial pipeline. Reuse existing visual language and canonical inbox/opportunity policies. Do not invent a parallel CRM, bypass qualification, or weaken external-action guardrails.
deliverables: A responsive website workflow-intake form with concise, human wording and no sensitive-file upload.
A locally testable first-party submission endpoint or adapter appropriate for the existing Cloudflare Pages architecture.
Durable submission and attribution records that can be reconciled into the canonical JVT opportunity and commercial pipeline.
Control-panel conversion metrics for form views or starts when observable, completed submissions, qualified submissions, and service interest.
Focused validation covering malformed input, duplicate submissions, internal/test submissions, qualification handoff, and no-send behavior.
A deployment brief that states the exact existing Cloudflare binding or configuration needed; do not publish or create paid infrastructure.
acceptance_criteria: Use the existing public-site design system and keep the form useful on desktop and mobile.
Collect only the minimum useful fields: name, public business email, company, workflow type or service interest, short problem description, and optional preferred next step.
Reject placeholders, obviously malformed addresses, JVT internal addresses, and duplicate submissions from conversion metrics.
Do not accept documents, credentials, payment data, protected health information, or other sensitive attachments.
Use one canonical submission identifier and make retries idempotent.
Integrate with the existing account, contact, opportunity, qualification, commercial, and control-panel paths rather than creating a second source of truth.
Do not send email, approve outreach, contact a submitter, publish the site, purchase services, create accounts, or make external commitments.
Run syntax checks, focused tests, local endpoint validation, and responsive visual validation before returning the result through architect-inbox.

roi_case.revenue_goal_link: Adds measurable inbound conversion to the March 2027 $10k cash-flow goal instead of relying only on outbound replies.
roi_case.expected_business_value: Turns site visitors into structured, attributable opportunities and gives E.G.G. a direct signal for preparing custom pilots.
roi_case.why_codex_is_worth_it: This crosses the public site, Cloudflare-compatible request handling, canonical CRM reconciliation, testing, and control-panel reporting.
roi_case.success_metric: A local end-to-end test submission appears once in the canonical opportunity pipeline and conversion dashboard without triggering an external message.
roi_case.fallback_if_not_run: Keep the epic queued and continue outbound operations; do not deploy a partial or untracked form.

safety_boundary: Repository-scoped internal implementation and local validation only. No production publish, outreach delivery, packet approval, spending, account changes, sensitive-data collection, market orders, crypto activity, provider enablement, destructive broad file actions, or external commitments.
